ng_guide.text: Newgrange: built about 3200 BC, with roughly 200,000 tonnes of stone and earth. That's five hundred years older than the Great Pyramid and a thousand older than Stonehenge.
The white quartz on the front was brought from Wicklow, sixty-odd miles off, and the grey stones from the Boyne. On a bright day, the whole thing glitters like a very big, very old iPhone.

lottery_winner.text: Every year around 30,000 people enter the lottery for the winter solstice. Fifty get in, two at a time. I'm the first Munster winner since 1994.
You stand in the dark, and then a thin line of gold comes down the passage. They say it's just the sun. I say it's still astonishing.

ng_farmer.text: My family's farmed beside this tomb for generations. We found stones in the field every year. Mostly we put them back. They looked cross.
There are three tombs: Newgrange, Knowth and Dowth. Knowth has more carved stones than all the rest of Europe's. I've only half the facts, but I've all the pride.

ng_archaeologist.text: Professor O'Kelly led the dig and rebuilding in the 1960s and 70s. The quartz wall's controversial, but I'm told the roof really does keep out the rain.
After five thousand years, only one thing's had to be fixed: the roof of the passage. The Neolithic builders would be insulted.

spiral_kid.text: There are three spirals joined at the middle, on the big stone at the door. I drew it on my hand with a pen. Mam says I'm not allowed near the stones.
I think it's a map. Or a bus route. Or the world's first doodle.
